title: Nivona CafeRomatica 8xx Review: Two-cup cappuccino at one touch, barista-style sequencing, and real recipe memory in a compact, serviceable platform

bodyHtml:

Typical EU list around €999; promos dip lower. UK pricing for NICR 825 often lands mid-£hundreds on sale.

Nivona CafeRomatica 8 Series

Rating 4.2 / 5 ★★★★★ ★★★★★
Two milk drinks at once Cappuccino-Connaisseur Aroma Balance (3 profiles) My Coffee: 10 recipes Removable brew group Bluetooth app support

Two-cup cappuccino at one touch, barista-style sequencing, and real recipe memory—packed into a compact, quiet, serviceable platform.

Overview

Nivona’s CafeRomatica 8 Series is the barista-coded superautomatic: brew two cappuccinos at one touch, choose milk/coffee sequence like a pro, pick from three Aroma Balance brew profiles that truly change extraction, and save up to ten “My Coffee” recipes. You still get a removable brew group, guided cleaning, and a calm dial-driven UI—with Bluetooth support on current trims.

Pros

  • Two cappuccinos/latte macchiatos at once (DUOplus)
  • Cappuccino-Connaisseur sequencing: milk-first, coffee-first, or together
  • Aroma Balance (Dynamic/Constant/Intense) = real flavor control
  • Up to 10 stored recipes with live programming
  • Removable brew group + guided cleaning routines

Cons

  • Grinder uses macro steps (not micrometric)
  • App is useful but basic
  • Focused menu—fewer “icon zoo” drinks than some rivals
  • Pricing/stock vary by specialist retailer & region
Key Features
  • Format: bean-to-cup with OneTouch milk; two-cup milk drinks on the 8 Series
  • Aroma Balance System: Dynamic / Constant / Intense brew profiles
  • Cappuccino-Connaisseur: choose milk-first, coffee-first, or both together
  • OneTouch SPUMATORE DUOplus: two cappuccinos/latte macchiatos at one press
  • “My Coffee” memory: up to 10 custom recipes
  • Water/beans: 1.8 L tank, 250 g hopper; bypass chute
  • Grinder: quiet conical burr; multiple macro steps
  • Strength/Temp: 5 aroma steps, 3 coffee temps; pre-brewing logic
  • Hot water: multi-temp on trims like NICR 825 (tea-friendly)
  • Controls: color TFT + rotary dial; Bluetooth app on current 8 Series
  • Power/Pump: ~1465 W heater; pump rated up to 15 bar
  • Size/weight: ~240 W × 330–340 H × 480 D mm; ~11–12 kg
  • Maintenance: removable brew group, CLARIS filter, guided cleans
Pricing & Variants
  • Common trims: NICR 820 and NICR 825 (stainless front + cup heating on 825)
  • EU list typically around €999; promos dip below depending on retailer/finish
  • UK: NICR 825 frequently hits mid-£hundreds on sales
  • Note: The newer “8000 Series” (big touch, 5 aroma profiles) is a separate platform—not this 8 Series
Who It Is For
  • Households drinking cappuccinos/latte macchiatos daily (two at once = faster mornings)
  • Users who want flavor control beyond “stronger,” via real brew profiles
  • Families who appreciate removable brew groups and guided maintenance
  • Tea drinkers (multi-temp hot water), and anyone who likes a sane dial-driven UI
Who Should Avoid It
  • Tinkerers demanding micrometric grind & ultra-granular control
  • Shoppers seeking giant touch UIs with dozens of animated presets
  • Those who prefer big-box buying over specialist retailers
FAQs
Does it make two milk drinks at once?
Yes. DUOplus dispenses milk foam for two cups and finishes both with espresso automatically.
What’s Cappuccino-Connaisseur?
Per-recipe control of milk/coffee order: milk-first, coffee-first, or together—affects taste and layering.
How many recipes can I save?
Up to 10 “My Coffee” recipes on 8 Series trims; you can live-program while brewing and save.
Is the brew group removable?
Yes—weekly rinse under warm water keeps flavor consistent and maintenance simple.
What’s the difference vs “8000 Series”?
8000 Series is a newer, different platform (bigger touch, more aroma profiles). This review covers the CafeRomatica 8 Series.

The Nivona CafeRomatica 8xx family is the most “barista-coded” set of superautomatics that still behaves like a normal home appliance. This series lets you brew two cappuccinos or two latte macchiatos simultaneously, pick the cappuccino sequence like a pro, and store up to ten custom “My Coffee” recipes. Nivona’s Aroma Balance System gives you three brew profiles that actually change extraction character rather than just turning up strength. The 8xx machines keep the brew group removable, the cleaning routine guided, and the interface sensible with a color display and rotary dial. Bluetooth control through the Nivona app is available on current 8xx variants. If you want a compact bean-to-cup with real control over flavor and milk flow, the 8xx is a sweet spot.

At a glance

  • Format. Bean-to-cup superautomatic with OneTouch milk. Two milk drinks at once on 8xx.
  • Aroma Balance System. Three brew profiles that change flow and contact time: Dynamic, Constant, Intense.
  • Cappuccino-Connaisseur. Choose milk-first, coffee-first, or both together for cappuccino sequencing.
  • OneTouch SPUMATORE DUOplus. Two cappuccinos or latte macchiatos at one press.
  • Recipe memory. Up to 10 custom “My Coffee” recipes on key 8xx models.
  • Capacities. Water tank 1.8 L, beans 250 g, pump rated up to 15 bar.
  • Controls. Color TFT plus rotary dial; Bluetooth app support on current 8xx product listings.
  • Maintenance. Removable brew group, CLARIS filter, guided cleaning cycles.

Glanceable specs

These are the common denominators across the CafeRomatica 8xx line. Individual trims vary slightly by finish and extras.

  • Dimensions and weight. About 240 W × 330–340 H × 480 D mm, 11–12 kg depending on trim.
  • Water and beans. 1.8 L removable tank, 250 g hopper with bean sensor on select SKUs.
  • Grinder. Quiet conical burr, multiple macro steps; “extra quiet operation” called out by Nivona.
  • Brew logic. Pre-brewing, Aroma Balance System with three profiles, five strength steps, three coffee temperatures.
  • Milk. OneTouch SPUMATORE DUOplus. Rinse and clean prompts for the milk path. Two-cup milk drinks supported.
  • Memory. Up to 10 user recipes on 8xx, live programming while brewing.
  • Connectivity. Bluetooth control via Nivona app on current 8xx pages; app available for iOS and Android.
  • Power. 1465 W heater, pump up to 15 bar.

Build and design

The 8xx series carries the “classic Nivona” look: clean lines, a color TFT display, and a sturdy rotary dial that does most of the heavy lifting in menus. In hand, the machines feel tighter than the price tag suggests. Panels fit well, the drip tray rides true, and the spout assembly glides up and down without wobbling. The stainless-front 825 trim looks and wears better than painted shells, and it includes niceties like a real cup-heating rack. The owner’s manual even calls out that automatic cup heating is an 825-only feature, a helpful tell that the company sweats details instead of pretending every trim is identical. 

Footprint lands in the friendly zone for modern kitchens at roughly 24 cm wide and 48 cm deep. Height is around 33 to 34 cm depending on trim. At about 11 to 12 kilograms, you can slide the machine forward for cleaning without recruiting help. These numbers track with multiple 8xx product listings and the 825 technical summaries. 

Nivona places the water tank on the left under a lid, the hopper on the right, and the bypass chute under the same top cover. The back-rollers are a humble win. They let you pivot the machine easily for access without drag marks. That kind of low-drama design is why these units end up in family kitchens rather than hobby benches.

You interact with the 8xx through a color TFT and physical keys. The screen is clear in bright kitchens and the rotary encoder is accurate enough to make recipe edits painless. Nivona’s UI is straightforward: choose the drink, tap the right arrow to step through aroma, volume, and milk, confirm with the dial. There is an honest, appliance-like clarity here that outlasts touch-screen gimmicks.

Bluetooth is available on current 8xx listings and backed by the company’s app in the iOS and Android stores. The app is basic compared with some competitors, yet it covers the useful stuff: recipe edits, maintenance prompts, and guidance. That is exactly what owners use after the honeymoon period. 

Workflow

The morning cadence

Start-up triggers an automatic rinse that warms the path and keeps the spouts fresh. Pick Espresso, Coffee, Cappuccino, or Latte Macchiato. The 8xx series can prepare two milk drinks at once, which matters on school mornings when two cappuccinos beat one cup and a queue. Nivona calls the dual-milk logic “OneTouch SPUMATORE DUOplus,” and it is a genuine differentiator at this price point. 

Live programming and “My Coffee”

Nivona’s “live programming” lets you edit a drink while brewing: you can tweak aroma and volume on the fly, then save the results as a new preset. The series also supports storing up to ten “My Coffee” recipes on key 8xx models. That is the difference between “we fiddled for a week” and “everyone has a button.” Factory recipes can be overridden, then restored if you regret the experiment. 

Strength, temperature, and profiles

Strength and temperature behave as you expect: five aroma steps raise dose and grind time, while three temperature steps bias finish and mouthfeel. The Aroma Balance System is the interesting lever. The three brew profiles change contact time and flow behavior rather than just pumping longer. With the same bean, same strength, and same volume, Dynamic, Constant, and Intense produce clearly different cups. That kind of change is rare in this segment, and it is the backbone of Nivona’s flavor story.

App rhythm

With Bluetooth enabled, the app mirrors key settings and provides a tidy maintenance agenda. It will nudge you about the filter and cleaning cycles, which is exactly how you keep taste and reliability from sliding. The app does not turn the 8xx into a remote café, yet it cuts down on panel time and helps new owners avoid the usual pitfalls. 

Espresso performance

What the machine is tuned to do

You are working with a conical burr grinder, pre-infusion, a removable brew group, and a brew profile system that alters the hydraulic recipe. On medium roasts, the 8xx is steady and surprisingly expressive for a superautomatic. With strength at 3 of 5, temperature on the middle step, and the profile set to Constant, you get round sweetness, balanced bitterness, and enough crema to satisfy the eye without turning the cup into foam. Nivona’s own literature ties the profile names to flavor outcomes, and independent retailer materials explain the logic in plain terms.

Dynamic softens the hit by easing the flow profile. Fruity blends and lighter roasts benefit here. Constant is the everyday choice for chocolatey medium roasts. Intense pushes contact time and extraction for a stronger presence with a darker bean. These are not placebo toggles. They move the extraction in sensible ways for home cups. The advantage is obvious if you rotate between two house coffees and do not want to re-dial the grinder every time.

Dialing a new coffee

Start with strength at 3 of 5, temperature at the middle step, and Constant. Taste. If your shot leans thin and sharp, go one grind step finer or shift from Dynamic to Constant or Intense before raising strength. If it is tight and bitter at short volumes, back to Constant or Dynamic, then open the grind one click. The point is to use the profile system to steer contact time first, then tune grind for flow, and lean on strength for presence. This hierarchy maps to how the 8xx is built.

Double shots

Two espressos in one go are not a single stretched pull. The machine grinds twice, which keeps flavor balanced in both cups. Nivona documents the two-cup sequence logic in the 8 series manual. The double-grind behavior matters if you run back-to-backs on weekends.

Long coffee and Americano

Use the Coffee program when you want a larger cup brewed through the group. For very large mugs, pull an espresso and add hot water from the menu. Three hot-water temperature steps are available on 8xx trims like the 825, which helps tea drinkers too. 

Milk steaming and texture

DUOplus is the headline

OneTouch SPUMATORE DUOplus can dispense milk foam for two cups and finish both drinks with espresso. It is a non-trivial quality-of-life upgrade if two people drink cappuccinos every morning. The foam quality is classic automatic frother texture: fine-bubbled and stable, biased toward cappuccino rather than silky, pourable latte art microfoam. For latte macchiato, the separation is clean and repeatable. 

Cappuccino-Connaisseur

Baristas sequence cappuccino by putting coffee in first so the milk can wrap around it. Superautomatics rarely let you pick that order. Nivona bakes the choice in. You can program milk-first, coffee-first, or both together. It sounds small until you taste two cups side by side. Coffee-first presents a tighter, more integrated cup. Milk-first will taste lighter. Being able to choose per recipe is the trick.

Plant milks and cup size

The system plays well with barista-formulated oat and soy milks. Oat produces a creamier texture. Soy holds foam a bit firmer. Almond trends lighter. If you switch milks, rinse the milk path immediately after service to avoid flavor carryover. The 8xx machines prompt you to do the right thing, which is why owners keep milk quality consistent. 

Cleaning the milk path

After milk drinks, the panel offers a fast rinse and later a deeper clean. Nivona highlights “convenient milk system cleaning” for the 8 series and includes rinse prompts for the OneTouch SPUMATORE. This workflow is the difference between carafes that get sticky by month two and carafes that keep producing stable foam all year.

Maintenance and reliability

Removable brew group

Pull the service door, press the latches, rinse the group under warm water, air-dry, reinstall. That is weekly hygiene you control with your own hands. It is one of the quiet strengths of Nivona’s design and a practical long-term advantage over sealed-group ecosystems. Retailers and manuals call out the removable group explicitly. 

Filters, hardness, and descaling

Set water hardness in the menu using the test strip. Fit a CLARIS filter when needed and follow the panel prompts for rinses, clean, and descale. The 8xx machines walk you through each step. Good water care shortens descale time and keeps the hydraulic path clean, which is why you punctually get the cup you expect. 

App-assisted maintenance

The Nivona app surfaces maintenance counters, filter timing, and cleaning checklists. It does not do anything magical, yet it helps households follow the boring schedule that keeps these machines reliable. If your machine lives in a busy kitchen, that nudge is worth real taste. 

Power, pump, and noise

Spec sheets place the heater around 1465 W with a pump rated up to 15 bar. Grind noise is restrained on the current 8xx, and Nivona calls out “extra quiet operation” on its series page. Noise is subjective, but in a tiled kitchen at 6 a.m., quiet matters. 

Real numbers you can trust

  • Water tank. 1.8 liters, removable.
  • Bean hopper. 250 grams with bean sensor on select trims.
  • Two-cup logic. Supported for espresso, coffee, and cappuccino or latte macchiato through DUOplus.
  • Recipe memory. Up to 10 “My Coffee” drinks.
  • Brew profiles. Aroma Balance System with 3 profiles.
  • Strength and temp. 5 aroma steps, 3 temperature steps.
  • Power and pump. About 1465 W heater, up to 15 bar pump rating.
  • Display. Color TFT with rotary dial.
    Numbers above are consolidated from the 8 series catalog, NICR 825/820 technical sheets, and retailer listings.

Deep dive: flavor control with Aroma Balance and Connaisseur

The Aroma Balance System is not a marketing flourish. It changes the extraction pattern so that the same bean at the same dose tastes meaningfully different. Dynamic lowers perceived bite and highlights gentle fruit and acidity. Constant balances sweetness and structure for daily blends. Intense pushes toward a stronger, more robust finish for darker roasts. It is a clean, three-lane road for households that share the machine and drink more than one coffee type. Nivona’s catalog describes the intent clearly, and several retailers expand the definitions in plain language.

Cappuccino-Connaisseur adds the missing piece for milk drinkers. Barista-style cappuccino relies on coffee first, milk second. Cafe-style sequences vary. Nivona lets you pick the order per recipe. That means you can save a barista-style cappuccino for yourself and a milk-first version for your partner without drama. It is a small feature that drives ownership satisfaction because it shows up in every cup.

Workflow details that matter in a family kitchen

Two at once

Two milk drinks at once is not a party trick. It halves the wait on weekdays. The machine grinds twice when you brew two espressos or two coffees. You are not just stretching a single extraction. The manual spells out the two-cup routine, including how the grinder cycles and how the machine behaves if the hopper or tank runs empty mid-sequence.

Live programming in practice

The “live” part is underrated. You can change aroma, volume, and total quantity during a brew. If you like the result, save it as “My Coffee.” If you do not, the factory settings are one reset away. It is safer than digging into menus blind and hoping your partner tolerates the experiment. 

Hot water that respects tea

Three temperature steps on the hot water tap are useful for green and oolong teas that do not want a rolling boil. The spec tables call this out for the 8xx. If you drink both coffee and tea, the feature is more than a footnote. 

Competitive comparisons

Jura E6 and E8

E6 is a cappuccino-first machine with a tight drink list. E8 adds one-touch flat white and latte macchiato and a larger screen. Jura uses a sealed brew group with detergent cycles rather than a removable group. If you want a sealed, guided maintenance approach and the most polished UI, Jura’s E8 is the step. If you want a removable brew group and two cappuccinos at once with cappuccino sequencing, the 8xx has the edge. Keep in mind that Jura’s app connectivity on midrange models typically requires an accessory, while Nivona lists Bluetooth on current 8xx pages. 

Philips 5400 LatteGo

Philips wins the milk-cleanup race. LatteGo is a tube-free, two-piece carafe that rinses in seconds and is dishwasher-friendly. Philips also offers four user profiles on that model. Where Nivona pulls ahead is flavor control. Aroma Balance and Cappuccino-Connaisseur allow more deliberate cups, and two-up cappuccinos are rare at this price. If your highest priority is frictionless milk cleanup, Philips is strong. If you want extraction control and two cappuccinos at once, Nivona is the better fit.

De’Longhi Dinamica Plus

Dinamica Plus brings a 3.5-inch touch display, profiles, and a very consistent LatteCrema carafe. It is a high-value rival with a deep drink list on some codes. Nivona responds with a removable brew group, dual-milk output on one touch, a more deliberate flavor system, and saved recipes that feel closer to barista presets than broad “stronger” buttons.

Gaggia Magenta Prestige and Cadorna Prestige

Gaggia’s removable group and carafe-based milk systems are comparable to Nivona’s service model. Magenta and Cadorna push screen-forward UIs and longer drink catalogs. Nivona’s 8xx answers with the two-cup milk feature, cappuccino sequencing, and a cleaner, dial-centric interface. If you want lots of one-touch icons and profiles, look at Gaggia. If you want a smaller set of drinks with better control over how they extract and layer, the 8xx is smarter.

Pricing, variants, and regional notes

Nivona sells through specialist retailers rather than broad marketplaces, and pricing floats by finish and channel. The NICR 820 and NICR 825 are the most common trims in the 8xx line. List prices in the EU often center around 999 EUR for the 8xx family, with retailer promos dipping below that. UK promotional pricing for the NICR 825 routinely appears in the mid-hundreds of pounds at peak sales. Check the exact code on the box and verify what is bundled. The stainless 825 adds stainless front and cup heater and is a safe pick if you want the nicest fit and finish in the series. 

Important note on naming. Nivona also launched an “8000 Series” platform in 2024 with a new design language, larger touch display, and even more aroma profiles. That is separate from the “8 Series” CafeRomatica models covered here. If you see a wide-screen touch panel and five aroma profiles, you are not looking at the older 8xx CafeRomatica machines. 

Scores

  • Build quality: 8.4
  • Grinder quality: 8.0
  • Espresso quality: 8.1
  • Milk system performance: 8.4
  • Workflow and ergonomics: 9.0
  • Cleaning and maintenance: 8.8
  • App and connectivity: 7.8
  • Value: 8.5

Overall: 8.4

Why these numbers: dual milk drinks at one touch, real flavor control via profiles, a removable group, and a sane UI deliver above-class usability. The grinder is solid for a superautomatic. The app is useful but not a centerpiece.

Build

The 8xx chassis is an example of quiet engineering. Nivona puts rigidity where it matters and keeps dress panels simple. The stainless 825 trim looks and cleans up better, and the 825-only cup heating rack is a small but satisfying extra. Inside, the layout is owner-serviceable: brew group behind a side door, tank under a top lid, bypass chute for pre-ground. Back-rollers save you from scraping the countertop when you pivot the machine. These are the things that make people keep using a machine every day.

The display-plus-dial workflow is fast to learn and hard to beat. Big icons, a clear status bar, and a positive-feeling encoder make for short programming sessions. The two-cup logic for espresso, coffee, and milk drinks is laid out cleanly in the manual and behaves predictably in practice. Grind cycles double for two cups instead of stretching a single extraction. That protects flavor and repeatability.

Workflow

Setup

Program water hardness with the test strip, select whether you will use a CLARIS filter, and run the guided steps. From there, pick the default coffee temperature and strength. The panel invites you to create “My Coffee” presets in real time instead of diving into nested menus. Owners actually do it because it is quick.

Daily use

Rinse at start, brew, rinse milk after the last cappuccino. Empty the dregs bin and drip tray at day’s end. The machine tells you what to do and when. It is not a diva. It is a well-behaved appliance with a few tricks up its sleeve. 

Family routine

Give each person a “My Coffee” preset rather than sharing a global “strong” button. Set cappuccino to coffee-first for the person who wants more definition and milk-first for the person who likes a softer cup. If two people drink cappuccinos at the same time, use DUOplus. Done. 

Espresso performance

The 8xx does steady, balanced espresso with less fuss than most machines in this bracket. The removable brew group rinses clean, so taste drift is minimal. The grinder holds settings without skating between marks. Pre-brewing keeps short shots from feeling hollow. The three aroma profiles matter most when you rotate beans. The Dynamic profile is a lifeline for lighter roasts that risk tilting sour at home brew temps. Constant is the sweet-spot for middle-of-the-road blends. Intense gives dark roasts the push they need without cranking strength into bitterness. You can hear the difference in extraction cadence and you can taste it.

Long coffees are clear and comfortable in the cup. If you enjoy really big mugs, the Americano workflow keeps extraction inside a sane window by adding water post-brew. Since hot water offers multiple temperatures, tea drinkers get their own quality of life upgrade without buying a kettle. 

Milk steaming

The DUOplus frother is designed for reliability and speed. Foam volume is right for cappuccino and latte macchiato. Temperature is serviceable with dairy and barista-formulated plant milks. The rinse prompts are short enough that people actually run them. You can go from two cappuccinos to a clean milk path in under a minute, which is what keeps foam quality from degrading month to month. The Connaisseur sequencing is a genuine differentiator for taste preference. Most superautomatics do not let you choose. Nivona does, and it sticks per recipe. 

Maintenance

What to do daily

Empty the drip tray and dregs bin. Run the milk rinse after the last milk drink. Wipe the spouts. The screen will ask at the right times. This is easy because it is short. 

Weekly and monthly

Pull the brew group, rinse, and let it air-dry. Fit a CLARIS filter if your water dictates it. Run the deeper milk clean with cleaner when the panel prompts. Execute descale on schedule. The menu exposes statistics so you can see usage and plan supplies. It is routine, not ritual.

Parts and consumables

Water filters, milk hoses, brew groups, and trays are widely available from specialty retailers. That parts ecosystem is part of why Nivona machines keep running in family kitchens instead of getting abandoned over a $3 gasket. 

Who it is for

  • Households that drink cappuccino and latte macchiato daily and want two-cup milk service
  • People who care about extraction character and want more than just a “stronger” button
  • Families that prefer a removable brew group and guided routines over sealed-group ecosystems
  • Buyers who want a clean, rotary-driven interface rather than a touchscreen that ages fast
  • Tea drinkers who benefit from multiple hot-water temperatures on the same machine

Trade-offs to expect

  1. Macro grinder steps. You steer taste with profiles and strength first. Experienced tinkerers may wish for finer grind gradations.
  2. No giant icon zoo. The menu is focused. If you want a thousand presets and animations, other brands will indulge you.
  3. App is practical, not fancy. It handles recipes and maintenance, then gets out of the way.
  4. Distribution through specialists. Inventory and pricing vary by region. Expect to shop specialty retailers rather than big-box listings.

Final verdict

The Nivona CafeRomatica 8xx does the quiet things right. It brews two cappuccinos at once with real texture. It lets you set cappuccino order like a barista so the cup tastes the way you prefer. It offers three brew profiles that actually change extraction. It stores ten real recipes so the people you live with stop changing your settings. It keeps the brew group removable so taste and reliability do not hinge on a bottle of detergent and a promise.

If you need more razzle-dazzle on the screen, there are flashier options. If you want an honest machine that tilts toward barista logic inside a family-friendly appliance, this is it. The 8xx is one of the few superautomatics where “My Coffee” is not a slogan. It is a reason to buy the machine, learn it for a week, and then stop thinking about it while you enjoy better cups every day.

TL;DR

Nivona’s 8xx series gives you two cappuccinos at one touch, cappuccino sequencing that actually changes taste, three brew profiles that alter extraction, up to ten stored recipes, a removable brew group, and a clean dial-driven UI. If you want practical flavor control and real milk convenience without turning your kitchen into a control panel, this is the pick.

Pros

  • Two cappuccinos or latte macchiatos at one touch through DUOplus
  • Cappuccino-Connaisseur sequencing for milk-first or coffee-first cups
  • Aroma Balance System with three profiles that change extraction character
  • Up to ten “My Coffee” recipes with live programming
  • Removable brew group and guided cleaning with app nudges

Cons

  • Grinder uses macro steps rather than micrometric tuning
  • App is useful but basic
  • Focused menu rather than a huge one-touch catalog
  • Pricing and stock vary by specialist retailer and region

Variant notes and quick buyer tips

  • NICR 820 vs 825. Same platform. The 825 adds a stainless front and a cup-heating rack with auto-on scheduling. If you care about material quality and hot cups, the 825 is the nicer pick.
  • Check the box code. The 8xx CafeRomatica machines are different from the newer “8000 Series” platform with a bigger touch display and additional aroma profiles. If the photos show a large touch panel and five aroma profiles, that is the newer “8000,” not the 8xx in this review.
  • Typical EU pricing. Expect around 999 EUR list, with promos below that depending on finish and retailer. UK promos for the NICR 825 have landed in the mid-hundreds of pounds at sale peaks.
